name: Baker's yeast, fresh (compressed)
source: Fresh compressed Saccharomyces cerevisiae: illustrative proximate (per kg) water 700 g (~70%, typical compressed-yeast moisture), protein 130 g, carbohydrate (glycogen/mannan/beta-glucan cell wall) 130 g, fat 20 g, ash 20 g (food-science/brewing literature pattern for fresh baker's yeast).
notes: Standard elemental conversion factors as wheat-grain.json, except ash is weighted toward phosphorus and potassium, reflecting real yeast cytoplasm/cell-wall mineral content. origin/yeast.ts propagates this substance from a real sugar feed plus a mineral/nitrogen nutrient charge, respiring the remainder of the feed to CO2 via world/exchange.ts's respire() — the real aerobic industrial process, chosen (rather than anaerobic fermentation) because propagation for biomass, unlike leavening a dough, is run aerobically to maximise cell yield.
